completion_claim: I have statically accounted for the supplied report-to-validator-to-status route and its supplied additional branches. The previously missing consumer is now available. This is a bounded source conclusion, not an observed execution, authenticity finding or qualification of capture/read enforcement.
answer:
For the six supplied report cases, with the issued session and collected HEAD and the stipulated exact, matching-digest reads, the full dictionary returned by status._auditor_report supports the named manager use. Each of its completion and report_kind entries retains the entire validator result under validation. That companion data distinguishes missing, invalid, mismatch and valid, and retains the parsed declaration and identity comparisons for mismatch as well as valid. The outer value is populated only for valid declarations; a null outer value does not erase a mismatching auditor claim.

The claim entries carry attributed_to="auditor", a collection source and an explicit note that these are neither an observed process exit nor a maintainer judgment. The source computes no such exit or judgment. Validation status describes declaration checking against the supplied identities, not substantive truth or completed work. No required loss or unsupported promotion is established on this matching-byte route.

This conclusion requires inspecting the full entries, including validation, rather than only value. It is also narrower than saying every return classifies captured report content. A missing session or unavailable/digest-mismatched evidence returns a reason and no validation. With expected_digest=None, the consumer validates synthetic empty bytes and sets source=null: its missing status is not an observation that a read report lacks a declaration. The evidence_tampered reason also combines unavailable bytes and digest mismatch; it does not establish actual tampering. These limitations are accounted for below. No consumer repair is established as necessary for the named use under the supplied matching-byte assumptions.

support.text:
Source coordinates refer to revision 5f00082d86768368478ed7cc85b52dd56a60255b. consumer-source.txt is the activated release excerpt of src/stewart/status.py, original lines 73–94. Other references are the original subject packet.

status.py lines 78–82 construct two entries, completion and report_kind, each carrying attributed_to, source, note, value and supplied context. The claims helper computes value from declaration[field] only when a declaration was passed. At lines 92–93, the consumer actually calls session_declaration_expectations(record, collected_head) and then validate_report_declaration(data, expected=expected, sources=sources). At line 94 it passes a declaration to claims only if result["status"] == "valid", but always passes validation=result on this path. Thus each returned entry includes the full validator dictionary, including a mismatching declaration when the outer value is null. This is actual source data flow, not a conclusion based on the consumer's docstring alone.

In declaration-source.txt, report_declaration.py lines 161–170 construct five expectations from the supplied session and a sixth for the supplied collected HEAD. Each of the five has source "pinned session"; observed_checkout_commit has source "HEAD observed at collection". Lines 143–147 return missing or invalid with null declaration, empty comparisons and refusal diagnostics. Lines 150–158 return the parsed declaration for both valid and mismatch, with expected/observed/source/matches per comparison and identity_mismatch diagnostics where applicable. Those fields survive in each status claim entry's validation member.

The returned note explicitly says "the auditor's declaration; not an observed process exit or a maintainer judgment". The supplied consumer performs identity validation and field selection, with no process-exit or manager-verdict calculation. The claim values remain report-derived data; the validation result is separate checking context. Comparison source labels describe the furnished expectations and do not independently authenticate them.

support.role: Manually derived status-return distinctions for all supplied reports
support.text:
The following are static deductions, not executed or captured outputs. Assume ENTRIES.json's session_record and collected_head, name="hypothetical-collection", and the stipulated exact bytes with each listed matching expected digest. For every case below, both returned claim entries have attributed_to="auditor", source="collection hypothetical-collection REPORT.md", the explicit non-exit/non-judgment note and the validation dictionary described. C and K below mean result["completion"]["value"] and result["report_kind"]["value"]. V means the validation member present in each entry.

report-valid.md: C="complete", K="answer"; V.status="valid"; V.declaration retains those values; six matching identity comparisons; diagnostics empty.
report-mismatch.md: C=null, K=null; V.status="mismatch"; V.declaration still contains completion="complete" and report_kind="answer". V.comparisons.target_commit retains forty "a" characters expected, forty "f" observed, source="pinned session", matches=false. One identity_mismatch diagnostic names target_commit; the other five comparisons match.
report-missing.md: C=null, K=null; V.status="missing"; V.declaration=null, V.comparisons empty, diagnostic reason="missing". The prose saying work is complete is not promoted to a structured completion claim.
report-invalid.md: C=null, K=null; V.status="invalid"; V.declaration=null, V.comparisons empty, diagnostic reason="duplicate_key" for completion. Neither competing completion value is selected as a claim.
report-partial-null.md: C="partial", K=null; V.status="valid"; V.declaration retains report_kind=null; six matching comparisons; diagnostics empty. A null kind remains distinguishable from an invalid declaration through the companion validation result.
report-prose-variant.md: the same returned dictionary as report-valid.md under the same collection/session inputs, despite the changed ordinary commentary and different stipulated report digest. The consumer checks the matching digest but does not return it; the unchanged declaration governs the claim output.

These results preserve the requested distinctions somewhere in the returned dictionary. No requirement here makes prose, every digest or every input byte part of that dictionary.

support.role: Firing comparison, invariance and first-projection analysis
support.text:
Firing pair: report-valid.md versus report-mismatch.md differs only in target_commit, replacing the pinned forty "a" characters with forty "f" characters. The validator changes valid to mismatch and preserves the operands and source. At status.py line 94 the mismatching report's outer claim values become null, while validation.declaration retains the same completion/report-kind claims and validation.comparisons explains the mismatch. The first consumer projection is therefore visible, but it is not a loss of the required distinction in the full dictionary.

Missing/invalid pair: report-missing.md and report-invalid.md both have null outer values and null validation.declaration, yet their validation.status and diagnostic reasons distinguish absence from rejected repeated JSON keys. A reader of outer value alone would fail the named use; that is not the granted view of the entire return.

Invariance: report-valid.md and report-prose-variant.md have identical declaration bytes with different ordinary surrounding prose. Neither the validator nor the consumer turns that changed prose into a structured claim. Equality of these outputs is intentional for the stated use, not a guarantee that arbitrary additional fences or malformed surrounding bytes cannot affect parsing.

Explicit null also survives: report-partial-null.md is valid with report_kind=null. In the manually reasoned variant deleting that required member, report_declaration.py lines 110–111 would instead yield missing_field/invalid, which the consumer would retain under validation. This variant was not executed.

The parser does discard declaration contents after a parse/structural refusal, and status withholds outer values for nonvalid results. The required state distinction and its available diagnostics remain. No supplied requirement asks the manager to treat a rejected competing completion as a unique auditor claim, so this projection does not establish a violation of the named use.

support.role: Additional branch account, evidentiary limits and bounded stopping point
support.text:
Additional branches in consumer-source.txt:

record=None: lines 83–84 return two attributed entries with value=null and reason="session_unavailable", with no validation member. No report read or declaration classification occurs. The collection source string remains present, so it must not be taken as proof of a successful read.

record available, expected_digest=None: lines 85–87 set data=b"" and source=None without reading REPORT.md. Lines 92–94 then return null claim values with validation.status="missing", null declaration, empty comparisons and a missing diagnostic. This missing result concerns the empty surrogate passed to the parser. It does not prove that an existing captured report lacks a declaration. The null source distinguishes this branch from the matching-byte report-missing.md case, whose source is the named collection.

record available, expected_digest present, data=None or reported SHA-256 differs: lines 89–91 return null values with reason="evidence_tampered" and no validation. The return does not retain whether unavailable bytes or a digest mismatch triggered that branch. It consequently supports only a coarse failure-to-validate account, not an observation of actual tampering, intent, or the report's declaration state. These are distinct from the classified missing/invalid/mismatch/valid cases, not additional examples of them.

The presence of a valid status is conditional on the expectations supplied, not proof of auditor completion, report truth, process success or manager agreement. The source labels and matched hashes do not extend the boundary assumptions into an authenticity or access-enforcement claim. The question stipulates the read outcomes, so the unsupplied read_regular implementation is not a remaining prerequisite for this source-flow conclusion.

The release resolves the earlier missing-consumer premise by supplying the actual retained validation context and caller arguments. The named route and supplied branches are now accounted for statically; there is no further missing artifact needed for this bounded conclusion. To investigate read enforcement, higher-level selection or rendered presentation would require a separately widened question. No such execution or scope expansion was performed.
